title: DeepFlow request decomposer — accordion-first drilldown for traces and cost context
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design an accordion-first request drilldown workspace (DeepFlow) inside Redwood Console that prioritizes rapid forensic triage. The design must surface spans, an interactive timeline, correlation IDs, request metadata, and cost-per-request breakdowns while remaining compact enough to fit beside the Request List. The UX should also make rollout flags and fallback model variants visible when available. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop, interaction spec for engineers (expanded/collapsed states, keyboard navigation, aria roles), annotated handoff with token/cost labels and data surface requirements.
comments: 2026-03-04 — Asha Patel: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma (see attachments). The card-first drilldown was too wide; pivoted to accordion stack anchored to the right rail to preserve table density.
2026-03-06 — Marco Ruiz: Iterated on compact span rows; added visual cue for latency outliers (thin red underline) and a micro-legend for quantized durations.

2026-03-08 — Priya Menon (PM): Reviewed trade-offs. Asked for cost attribution per span in addition to request-level cost; flagged potential backend perf impact if we compute per-span costs on the fly. Requested a graceful degradation plan if cost data isn't available.

2026-03-09 — Kenji Nakamura (Eng, serving runtime): Raised a dependency: backend needs a light-weight aggregated token-cost payload in the request index to avoid fetching a heavy invoice per click. Suggested an API field 'token_cost_estimate' on the request summary. Also noted correlation IDs may be multiple — recommend UI show primary and toggle to reveal linked correlations.

2026-03-10 — Design critique with cross-functional reviewers: Positive feedback on in-rail accordion; concerns about discoverability of span-level stack traces. Action: add a one-click 'expand all spans with errors' control and a compact stack preview line with ellipsis.
2026-03-12 — Marco Ruiz: Prototype updated with keyboard focus order and aria-labels. Link to interactive prototype in attachments. Preparing engineering handoff doc.
2026-03-14 — Security review note (Lina Torres): Ensure any rollout flag values are redacted when user lacks feature-flag read permission. Add an entry to security_review_required.

2026-03-15 — Asha Patel: Merged final annotations; moving to In Review. Created checklist for QA: accessibility scan, mobile breakpoint behavior, empty-state for missing cost, and metric instrumentation for click-through rate on 'expand span' action.
decisions: Use right-rail accordion anchored to request list instead of modal to preserve context and speed of switching between requests.
Show token_cost_estimate at request header; compute per-span cost as derived UI approximation when backend per-span cost missing.
Expose primary correlation ID inline; add a toggle to reveal linked correlation graph and related requests.
Add "expand error spans" quick action; default collapsed spans to save vertical space.
Rollout flag values should only be visible to users with feature-flag read scope; otherwise show masked state with 'insufficient permissions' tooltip.
notes_for_engineering: Data expectations: request summary payload should include request_id, primary_correlation_id, start_time, duration_ms, token_count, token_cost_estimate, error_flags (boolean), rollout_flags_metadata (redacted for unauthorized users). UI should avoid per-click heavy fetches; fall back to a single 'fetch full trace' call when user opens 'Full Trace' action. Provide feature-flag gating for per-span cost exposure.
